rationale: Every run is limited by an I/O-port path at ss/100C/1.60V; reg-to-reg needs only ~4.2 ns, and port-path T_eff falls with the target because IO delays scale with the period, so keep period_frac 0.45. Hold, slew/cap and DRC are clean, with no congestion. At 0.45, T_eff tracks wirelength almost linearly (4,019-4,040 um: 5.95-6.05; 4,558: 6.36; 4,928: 6.70), and port nets run to edge pins, so test a ~11% smaller die: util 28 (util 30 ran fine; failures were at 38-40) with density_delta 18, keeping the best run's 46% density. Keep timing-driven placement, DELAY 3, slew margin 35% (port buffers) and post-GRT timing/design repair for tight re-runs. Routability is unpinned; history favours off.
